Shatili

A stone fortress-village in Khevsureti on the Chechen border — one of the most striking places in the Caucasus.

Time needed
4 h
From Tbilisi
155 km · 4:30
Road
4x4 only
Car needed
Off-road 4x4
Season
June–September
Entry
~5 ₾

Shatili is not a collection of houses but a single grown organism. On the northern edge of Khevsureti, in the Arghuni gorge, some fifty stone towers and dwellings are built into and onto each other on a steep slope. They rise in terraces, one roof serving as another's yard, and together they form an indivisible defensive system: in the Middle Ages the entire village was one fortress.

Most of the structures date from the 9th to the 13th century. For centuries the Khevsurs held this frontier against raids from the north, and Shatili was its last outpost. In the 1950s the population was forcibly resettled to the lowlands; today the village is partly inhabited again and several towers have been converted into guesthouses.

Around Shatili:

  • The Anatori crypts, 3 km away, stone tombs where plague victims are said to have walked in to die rather than infect the village
  • Mutso, another fortress-village 12 km further on, wilder and almost entirely abandoned
  • The Arghuni gorge itself, narrow, deep and within the border zone

This is one of the remotest places in Georgia that you can still drive to, and staying overnight is close to obligatory: doing it as a day trip from Tbilisi is punishing.

Practical advice

The season is short — mid-June to late September, since the Datvijvari Pass at 2,676 m is snowbound the rest of the year. Book accommodation ahead: Shatili has only a handful of guesthouses and they fill in August. There is essentially no mobile signal and no ATM, so bring cash. It is a border zone, so a passport is required. Pack warm clothing even in August, when nights drop to five or eight degrees.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi take the Military Highway to Zhinvali, then turn right towards Barisakho up the Aragvi valley. Asphalt continues to Barisakho; after that comes roughly 60 km of gravel over the Datvijvari Pass — narrow, unbarriered, with steep descents and loose rock. In total 155 km and at least four and a half hours, more after rain. Only a proper 4x4 with good tyres belongs on this road; an ordinary crossover is a gamble. Take your last fuel at Zhinvali or Barisakho, as there is no station in Shatili.

Nearby places

Monastery

Gergeti Trinity Church

A 14th-century church at 2,170 m with Mount Kazbek behind it — the single most recognisable view in Georgia.

Waterfall

Dariali Gorge and the Gveleti Waterfalls

The narrowest gorge in the Caucasus, right at the border, with two waterfalls and a short, dramatic trail.

Mountain

Omalo and Tusheti

Georgia's most isolated mountain region, beyond the Abano Pass — 4x4 only, and only from June to October.
